segments.title: Force K as a heavy raider-hunting force
segments.summary: In 1939, Force K combined HMS Renown, HMS Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers as a heavy anti-surface raider-hunting group.
segments.body: Force K was a heavy Royal Navy force for hunting surface raiders in 1939. The battlecruiser HMS Renown and the aircraft carrier HMS Ark Royal were its principal ships. H-class destroyers accompanied them. Ark Royal's aircraft and Renown's speed and guns gave the group several ways to intercept a raider.

evidence.note: The transcript calls Force K a heavy anti-surface force and names Renown, Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers.
The later explanation links Ark Royal's aircraft with Renown's speed and guns in the planned interception of a surface raider.

segments.title: Reinforcing the River Plate hunt from Freetown
segments.summary: During the Battle of the River Plate crisis, Force K raced from Freetown to reinforce Harwood's squadron if Admiral Graf Spee broke out.
segments.body: Force K raced across the Atlantic to reinforce Commodore Harwood's squadron during the Battle of the River Plate crisis. The aim was to provide heavier ships if Admiral Graf Spee tried to break out. Force K also offered a means of intercepting the raider after a successful escape. Its operating area was Freetown, rather than Gibraltar, and it had been positioned there for this heavy support role.

evidence.note: Force K crosses from Freetown to support Harwood if Graf Spee attempts a breakout or to intercept it after a successful escape. Freetown is explicitly identified as the operating area, rather than Gibraltar.

segments.title: How Force K planned to intercept a returning raider
segments.summary: Radio signals could guide Force K's search for a raider returning north, with Swordfish attacks intended to slow or sink it before Renown closed in.
segments.body: Force K's planned interception combined radio information with Ark Royal's aircraft and Renown's speed and guns. A surface raider returning from the South Atlantic to the North Atlantic would face both air attack and surface interception. With luck, radio signals would indicate where to look. Once the raider was found, Swordfish would attack, probably slowing it and possibly sinking it. Renown was expected to finish off a ship that survived the air attack.

evidence.note: The theoretical role combines Ark Royal's aircraft and Renown's speed and guns. Radio information depends on luck, Swordfish attacks would probably slow and might sink the raider, and Renown would finish the interception.

segments.title: How Force K changed after 1939
segments.summary: Force K named a raider-hunting group in 1939 and surface raiders in 1942, so the date matters when identifying its mission.
segments.body: The Force K name was reused for formations with different roles. The 1939 group combined Renown, Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers to hunt enemy surface raiders. The closing comparison identifies the 1942 Force K as a surface-raiding force. The date therefore matters whenever Force K appears in an account.

evidence.note: The closing comparison calls later forces different and identifies Force K in 1942 as surface raiders. The intervening date at 1:53 is transcribed as 1949 in an incomplete phrase, so no 1940 formation is inferred. Audio review of 1:53-2:00 is needed to resolve that phrase.
The opening identifies the 1939 anti-raider force as Renown, Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers.
